The description 'Fills a 2D slice of the voxel grid along one axis' confirms that slices are processed independently along the X, Y, or Z axis.

- If a slice contains no solid voxels, the entire slice is filled [S1, unofficial].

The evidence describes the logic for filling a 2D slice (e.g., FillYZ, FillXZ, FillXY). The algorithm scans from both ends towards the center. It sets bits in the buffer for empty space until it hits a solid voxel, at which point it stops that direction. If a slice contains no solid voxels, the forward scan will reach the end (e.g., `z` reaches `uz+1`) without hitting a solid voxel, and the backward scan will reach the start without hitting a solid voxel. Consequently, every voxel in that slice is set in the buffer, meaning the entire slice is filled.

- If a slice is entirely solid, the scan encounters a solid voxel immediately and no voxels are filled in that slice [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the algorithm 'sets bits in a buffer for empty space until it hits an existing solid voxel, then stops that direction.' It further details that for each slice (e.g., FillYZ, FillXZ, FillXY), the code iterates from both ends towards the center. If a solid voxel is encountered ('If solid, break forward scan' or 'If solid, break backward scan'), the loop breaks immediately. Consequently, if a slice is entirely solid, the very first voxel checked from either end is solid, causing the scan to break immediately without setting any bits (filling any voxels) in that slice.
